ROLE: Request that a running loop_run() return after the current event batch, without touching sessions, descriptors or queued output.

STRUCT.NAME: struct loop
STRUCT.ROLE: reactor whose internal stopped request is set

VAR.NAME: struct loop
VAR.ROLE: only the stopped field is written; the reactor, its broker and all sessions keep their ownership

LOGIC.ACTION: 1. If l == NULL return. 2. l->stopped = 1. No descriptor, buffer, session or registry is touched, so a stop request never truncates already queued output: loop_run() finishes dispatching the batch in progress, runs broker_reap() and mask_sync(), and only then observes the flag at the top of the next iteration and returns 0.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: void. A subsequent (or in-flight) loop_run() returns 0 after completing at most one more dispatch/reap/mask batch; sessions that still hold queued output stay registered for EPOLLOUT so the caller may choose to flush before tearing down.
INVARIANTS_USED: stopping is cooperative: the loop returns, and all cleanup (closing sessions, freeing buffers) is performed afterwards by ordinary code
a stop request must not discard queued output silently; it only ends the wait for more readiness
the loop object stays owned by the caller, which calls loop_destroy() afterwards
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: l is a live reactor or NULL.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: l->stopped == 1 (or nothing happened for a NULL argument); no other state changed.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Intended to be called from ordinary code in the same thread as loop_run(); setting an int flag is the only operation, so calling it from a signal handler would also be harmless but the design uses the sig_atomic_t flag for that.

runtime: loop_run running with one session that has 200000 bytes queued and a slow reader
